6.t: Harappan Sites and Decline | Ancient India, Simply Unearthed Ep 6
6.d:
The brush uncovers a small figure in bronze, slender and standing. It was cast by the lost-wax method: model it in wax, cover it in clay, melt the wax out, pour the metal in. Four and a half thousand years ago, somebody in this world knew how to do that. And then, within a few centuries, the cities they lived in emptied. Why did a world this capable empty out its own cities?

7.t: The Early Vedic Period | Ancient India, Simply Unearthed Ep 7
7.d:
Here is a strange thing. For the next four episodes, the ground gives us very little: a few post-holes, some plain pottery, no cities, no palaces. And yet we know more about what these people thought than about almost anyone else in the ancient world. Because they left something else entirely — a book, carried in memory for centuries before anyone wrote it down. How do we know so much about what these people thought, and so little about where they lived?

8.d:

29.t: Gupta Administration and Society | Ancient India, Simply Unearthed Ep 29
29.d:
